title: Reduction for a Longer Stay in Resort Lodging
content:
The length of a Resort Lodging stay in nights decides the length-of-stay reduction taken on the room rate, read against the threshold the unit type publishes.

Where the stay runs to at least twice the unit type's length-of-stay threshold in nights, the long stay reduction of 15 percent is taken.

Where the stay runs to at least the unit type's length-of-stay threshold but fewer than twice that threshold in nights, the unit type's length-of-stay reduction is taken.

Where the stay runs to fewer nights than that threshold, no length-of-stay reduction is taken.

## The threshold of each unit type, and twice it

| Unit type | Length-of-stay threshold (nights) | Twice the threshold (nights) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base Village Inn Room | 5 | 10 |
| Slopeside Studio | 5 | 10 |
| Slopeside One-Bedroom Residence | 7 | 14 |
| Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence | 7 | 14 |
| Mountain Lodge Suite | 7 | 14 |
| Summit Penthouse Residence | 7 | 14 |
| Private Mountain Chalet | 10 | 20 |

### The three tiers on a Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence (hypothetical stays)

The unit type's threshold is 7 nights and twice it is 14. A stay of 14 nights reaches twice the threshold, so the long stay reduction of 15 percent is taken. A stay of 13 nights falls short of twice the threshold but reaches the threshold itself, so the unit type's length-of-stay reduction is taken. A stay of exactly 7 nights likewise reaches the threshold and takes that same tier. A stay of 6 nights runs to fewer nights than the threshold, and no length-of-stay reduction is taken.
